summary: Algerian-born Alexandre Villaplane captained France at the first World Cup in 1930, fell into match fixing and crime, then led an SS-backed North African unit that tortured, robbed and massacred civilians in occupied France until his execution in 1944.

evidence.note: 1827 fly-whisk incident opens the long segment on the French conquest of Algeria
about 1.6 million Algerians killed in the first decades of French occupation
Villaplane born in Algiers on 24 December 1904 to a settler family
captains France at the first World Cup in Uruguay, 1930
masterminds match fixing and bribery at Antibes; the club is stripped of its title
jailed in 1935 for fixing horse races, drifts into Paris organized crime
Henri Lafont recruits criminals for the SS; gang based at rue Lauriston
North African Brigade formed with SS; Villaplane commands about 100 men
account of peasants beaten, set on fire and shot in front of a captive woman
detailed account of hostage executions and the Mussidan massacre of June 1944
captured August 1944, tried and shot by firing squad on 26 December 1944

notes: Primary theme could be nazism instead of sports; sports chosen because the title frames him as a footballer and themes.yaml lists this story under sports. Covered span starts in 1827 because the French conquest of Algeria fills most of part 1 and is listed as a secondary subject. military-officer reflects his SS lieutenant rank in an auxiliary unit.
